doc.title: Wendy Oxenhorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 22, 2026

title: Opening and adjectives for the Jazz Foundation work
summary: Monk Rowe introduces Oxenhorn as the Red Cross for veteran musicians and asks for adjectives; she says thrilling, challenging, exciting, creative.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive and I’m very, very pleased to have Wendy Oxenhorn with me today. And you’ve presented a bit of a challenge as far as an introduction because you’ve done an awful lot in your life. So I came up – I don't know why I saw this but I’m going to call you the Red Cross for veteran jazz and blues musicians. How’s that?
And roots, and R&B, soul and rock & roll too.

Right. That is sort of one of my questions we’ll get to, but you were a co-founder and founding director of the Jazz Foundation. And I want to start right off with can you come up with a couple adjectives that describe that experience of, from the very get-go when you arrived at this foundation to where you are now. How would you describe the experience?
Oh, adjectives. Thrilling, challenging, exciting, creative.
You know I had written down a couple and you had two that I wrote down, because I was just trying to put myself in your position. Was there ever melancholy involved?
